sources.locator: Section 1.8 'Locally finite (artinian) and finite abelian categories', printed pp.9-11 / PDF pp.26-28 (Definitions 1.8.1-1.8.14, Proposition 1.8.10, Corollary 1.8.11, Remarks 1.8.7, 1.8.9, 1.8.12, Proposition 1.8.15); Section 1.11 inspected only to place the deferred Deligne boundary

contents.name: Definition 1.8.1 and Remark 1.8.2: locally finite (artinian) k-linear abelian categories and the Jordan-Holder/Krull-Schmidt consequences
Definition 1.8.3 and Proposition 1.8.4: injective/surjective functors between locally finite categories and Schur's lemma over algebraically closed k
contents.reason: This pair proves the module realization without Schur's lemma and without assuming algebraic closure of k; the algebraically closed hypotheses are needed only by the abstract finite-linear-category statements deferred with the categorical Eilenberg-Watts development.

contents.name: Definition 1.8.5: a finite k-linear abelian category is one equivalent to A-mod for a finite-dimensional algebra A
Definition 1.8.6: the intrinsic finite definition (finite-dimensional Hom, finite length, enough projectives, finitely many simples)

The paragraph proving equivalence of Definitions 1.8.5 and 1.8.6: P = sum of projective covers P_i, A = End(P)^op, F = Hom_C(P,-) exact and faithful, any exact faithful F represented by a projective generator
Remark 1.8.7, duality part: the dual category of a finite abelian category is finite, and duality V -> V* is an equivalence between A-mod and A^op-mod
Remark 1.8.7, injective-hull clause: in a finite abelian category any object has a projective cover and an injective hull
contents.reason: Injective hulls are not used anywhere in this pair's statements or proofs; projective covers are supplied by the published finite-dimensional-algebra theorem, and the injective-hull half would need the opposite-category duality plus an existence theorem that belongs to the injective-resolution development.

contents.name: Definitions 1.8.8 and Remark 1.8.9: (tensor-)representable functors A-mod -> B-mod, and F is representable if and only if it has a right adjoint
Proposition 1.8.10: an additive k-linear F: A-mod -> B-mod is representable (F = V tensor_A -) if and only if it is right exact
Corollary 1.8.11: for a finite abelian k-linear category C an additive k-linear left exact F: C -> Vec is F = Hom_C(V,-) for some V
Remark 1.8.12: the Yoneda lemma identifies morphisms between representable functors Hom_C(V,-) and Hom_C(W,-) with morphisms W -> V
Displayed (1.7), K_0(C) on indecomposable projectives, gamma: K_0(C) -> Gr(C), and Definition 1.8.13 (virtual projective objects K_0(C) tensor_Z k)
contents.reason: Decomposition multiplicities, the Cartan homomorphism and virtual projective objects belong to the published Grothendieck-group and Cartan-pairing development, which already carries the K_0/G_0 theory of finite-dimensional algebras; this pair needs none of it.

contents.name: Definition 1.8.14: the Cartan matrix of a finite abelian category
contents.reason: The Cartan matrix is the matrix of the Grothendieck-group homomorphism gamma, which lives on the published Cartan-pairing page together with the dual-basis and decomposition-multiplicity machinery.

contents.name: Proposition 1.8.15: canonical algebra isomorphism for two exact faithful functors F_1, F_2 and the tensor product F_1 x F_2
contents.reason: The tensor-product algebra of functors is part of the Deligne-product and categorical-Eilenberg-Watts development; the design assigns the abstract finite-linear-category statements there, so it is not built here.

sources.title: Fuchs, Schaumann, Schweigert, Eilenberg-Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem, arXiv:1612.04561v3
sources.locator: Section 2.1 'Notation and background', pp.5-8 (Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2, Corollary 2.3, equations (2.1)-(2.3)); Sections 3.1-3.2, pp.14-17 (Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2 statement and proof structure) and Section 3.5, pp.22-24 inspected for the deferred boundary

contents.name: Section 2.1 standing conventions: finite-dimensional algebras, the categories A-mod, mod-A and B-bimod-A, and the equivalence of finite linear categories with finite-dimensional module categories
Lemma 2.1, parts (L1)-(L3): for k-linear F: A-mod -> B-mod, left exact <=> admits a left adjoint <=> F = Hom_A(M,-) with M = (F(A A*_A))*
Lemma 2.1, parts (R1)-(R4): for k-linear G: A-mod -> B-mod, right exact <=> admits a right adjoint <=> G = G(A A_A) tensor_A - <=> G = Hom_A(-, G(A A_A)*)*
Equation (2.1): Hom_A(A_X, (M_A)*)* = Hom_k(M_A tensor_A A_X, k)* = (M_A tensor_A A_X) and exactness of the duality (-)*: A-mod -> mod-A
Lemma 2.2(i): equivalence of Lex(A-mod, B-mod) with (A-bimod-B)^opp and of Rex(A-mod, B-mod) with (A-bimod-B)^opp, mapping F to (F(A A*_A))* and G to G(A A_A)*
Lemma 2.2(ii): equivalence Lex(A-mod, A-mod) -> Rex(A-mod, A-mod) sending the identity to (A A_A)* tensor_A - (the Nakayama correction triangle)
contents.reason: The equivalence between Lex and Rex is not the inclusion of exact functors and needs the explicit Nakayama correction; the design builds it with the categorical triangle in the Deligne-product pair.

contents.name: Corollary 2.3: the (L1)-(L3) and (R1)-(R3) equivalences for functors between general finite linear categories, and representability for target vect
contents.reason: The model-independent form for abstract finite linear categories (without choosing a module model) is exactly the content of the categorical Eilenberg-Watts development assigned to the Deligne-product pair.

contents.name: Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 (categorical Eilenberg-Watts): the triangle Lex(A,B) ~ A^opp x B ~ Rex(A,B) for finite k-linear categories, with the functors Phi_l, Phi_r, Psi_l, Psi_r
contents.reason: The abstract triangle over finite linear categories, with ends and coends and the Deligne product, is the subject of the Deligne-product pair; this pair only needs the algebra-level classification of Lemma 2.1.

contents.name: Section 3.5, Lemmas 3.15-3.16 and formulas (3.56)-(3.58): the Nakayama functors, the bimodule Radford S^4 theorem boundary and its categorical correction
contents.reason: The Nakayama correction and its derived/graded boundary are used by the graded-Eilenberg-Watts pair and the derived-boundary remark; this pair makes no claim about them.

contents.name: Section 4 applications (affine schemes, tensor-category Radford S^4)
contents.locator: pp.35-41 (not read as a proof source; scope checked from the introduction and contents)
contents.reason: The applications to algebraic geometry and to Radford S^4 for tensor categories are outside the homological-algebra scope of this pair and use structure (Hopf algebras, affine schemes) the library does not build on this page.
